title: Nine months bedridden: breaking the news to the band and losing money on the cars
summary: Back in the doctor's office he is told to lie flat for nine months, then tells his band in August 1947 and takes a loss on the cars.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, all right. We're back in the doctor's office now, and he told me, he said "You're not in your teens anymore and we're dealing with a bone situation, and nature takes a little longer to heal them." And so he said, and this is what hurt me -- "My advice to you is that you're gonna have to lay. I'm gonna operate, but my advice to you is that it's gonna be 9 months bedridden, or maybe longer if complications set in."
Boy, that's when the cryin' started. I got to go

through this again? Ben cried, I cried, the doctor cried, my wife in stone tears. So he said, "But I'll tell you this much; if you follow my instructions, in your condition that you're in right now, and I operate on you, I will guarantee you you will go back to your normal activity." Well, this was a lift.

And I got to go back uptown where my rehearsal is called, and let them know but when I go, I'll stop by and get a case of beer, a couple or three bottles of liquor ... I got my dark glasses on, and the sun is shining bright, in August, 1947 -- I'll give you the year. And had to go to the wives, and everybody was happy; they were counting the money for 3 months, but I couldn't make it. And got to tell them this.

And I bought 2 cars, and Bart bought the Desoto back and he was working out the office, and I took a loss on the Mercury. It was on a promissory note with Ben, but he had to get rid of them to get his money back. He had to shove it off on somebody. I took a loss on the Mercury. I had a '49 Mercury and a '48 Desoto convertible. Suburban.
